statement_en: Two papers claim that feeding live snails helps keep water quality in check, by preventing leftover bait from spoiling and water becoming too fertile, and by purifying the water. Both papers describe this in the context of river crab culture rather than mandarin fish, and neither gives measured results.

basis.summary: Both claims, from two separate papers, report the same reduction in ammonia-nitrogen excretion with no disagreement; C10694 is a measured result and so carries more weight, while C9696 is only claimed and mainly corroborates it.

statement_en: In mandarin fish, feeding a low-protein diet markedly reduced ammonia-nitrogen excretion, which the claims attribute to more of the dietary protein being used to build body protein rather than being lost through metabolism. Both papers point the same way, and the claims give no specific conditions.

basis.summary: Both claims, from two different papers, point the same way (worse water quality), but one is inferred and the other is reported background, so neither is a direct measurement; I therefore kept the wording general and found no disagreement to resolve.

statement_en: Both claims say that replacing fishmeal with plant protein worsened water quality: fish used the substitute feed poorly, and more nitrogenous waste, including ammonia nitrogen, was excreted into the water. The claims give no measured values or conditions, and neither reports a benefit or no effect.
statement_zh: 两条结论都认为，用植物蛋白替代鱼粉会加重水质问题：鱼对替代饲料利用率低，氨基酸不平衡和抗营养因子影响吸收，含氮废物（包括氨氮）排泄增多，污染水体。这两条都没有给出具体测定数据或条件，也没有提到有益或无影响的结果。

statement_en: Three papers claim that scheduled, quantified feeding (small, frequent meals, precise amounts, and stopping when fish stop competing for food) reduces uneaten feed and so helps keep water quality from deteriorating. These are stated claims only, with no measured water quality results or specific conditions given.
